usage: "L-3aila" is the standard word for family in Moroccan Darija, used across all regions in both casual and formal contexts. Another extremely common word is "l-famila", borrowed from French or Spanish, which is slightly more colloquial. When greeting someone, it is culturally expected to ask about the well-being of their family.

variants.label: my family
variants.note: Used when talking about your own family.

variants.label: your family
variants.note: Used when addressing a single person (male or female) about their family.

variants.label: colloquial alternative
variants.note: A very common loanword used interchangeably with l-3aila in casual speech.

variants.label: parents / household
variants.note: Literally 'owners of the house', used to refer to one's immediate family or parents living at home.

responses.english: They are fine, praise be to God.
Everyone is fine, may good things ask about you.

examples.english: I am going to travel with my family.
Say hello to your family for me.
